pending-clause.answer: Read §2002:8.8.1.1, 8.8.1.3.1 and 8.8.1.3.1.1 (standard intermediate data item, 'a precision of 32 decimal digits', rounding to 31; the PB5575 gap is the compiler's 34). They govern the evaluation of an arithmetic expression only. A single literal is not converted to a standard intermediate item because GR2 keeps it a literal; a 2002 literal has at most 31 digits, so the 32/31 versus 34 digit gap (PB5575) cannot reach it. No dependence.

behaviour-switch.answer: The switch (DialectBehavior.CompileTimeArithmeticImplementorDefined, src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Frontend/Expressions/CompileTimeArithmetic.cs#For) picks only the mode in which a compile-time arithmetic expression is evaluated: Standard at 2002, as §2002:7.2.5.2 GR1 requires ('Standard arithmetic shall be used for all arithmetic operations'). The rule is that a lone numeric literal is NOT an arithmetic expression, so neither the switch's mode nor §2002:7.2.5.2 GR2's truncation is applied to it. eval_basic.cob re-run now at --std 2002: GR2-OK (EVALUATE 1.5 matches WHEN 1.5) and ARITH-TRUNC-OK (1.5 + 0 truncates to 1, the Standard-mode expression path) (rerun.log).
